title: CFETs Forge Better Connections
gist: Intel, Samsung, TSMC, and IBM are converging on complementary FET (CFET) transistor stacking as the next major logic scaling step after gate-all-around, each taking a distinct integration approach, with production expected around 2031 and virtual fabrication/AI-driven simulation increasingly essential to manage atomic-level variation risk.

insights.claim: CFETs stack p-type and n-type transistors vertically instead of laterally, and are expected to nearly double transistor density versus today's lateral nanosheets while delivering a 40% packing density improvement, a 50% performance leap, and a potential 70% efficiency gain.
insights.speaker: Laura Peters
insights.so_what: These are the headline performance/density/power targets against which leading foundries (TSMC, Samsung, Intel) and IBM's licensee Rapidus will be benchmarked as CFET moves toward production; large deviations from these targets at any player would be a meaningful competitive signal.
insights.locator: In just a handful of years, the leading-edge device makers will begin rolling out CFETs

insights.claim: According to imec's roadmap, first CFET production is expected at the A7 node around 2031, with critical dimensions scaling below 18nm, and continued (though more modest) metal pitch shrinkage will rely on higher-NA EUV lithography.
insights.speaker: Laura Peters
insights.so_what: A 2031 production timeline gives investors a concrete horizon for when CFET-related capex (EDA tools, EUV lithography, ALD equipment) should ramp meaningfully across the industry.
insights.locator: Fig.1: The roadmap shows the first CFET production at the A7 node around 2031

insights.claim: CFETs are expected to reduce standard-cell height from about 5T (5x contacted pitch) to 4T or less, and the added density could enable SRAM designs to move from a 6T to a more compact 4F2 construction.
insights.speaker: Laura Peters
insights.so_what: SRAM area is often the binding constraint on AI accelerator die size (cache-heavy designs); a 6T-to-4F2 shift would be a significant potential area/cost win for AI chip designs once CFET matures.
insights.locator: Nonetheless, CFETs will likely reduce standard-cell height

themes.theme: Diverging integration approaches among the leaders

insights.claim: IBM is pursuing a sequential CFET process with slightly staggered (offset by 10nm) transistors that are fully fabricated before the second set, while most others (including Intel) are pursuing monolithic flows where the entire stack is built at once; TSMC uses backside gate contact plus two versions of vertical contact plugs for SRAM bit cells, and Samsung has developed a novel dielectric stack to separate the two gate regions.
insights.speaker: Laura Peters
insights.so_what: The four leading-edge players are placing genuinely different technical bets on CFET integration, meaning process risk and eventual manufacturability/yield outcomes could diverge significantly by vendor, a key differentiator for foundry customer selection in the early 2030s.
insights.locator: While process qualification is years off, early research shows TSMC, Intel, Samsung, and IBM

insights.claim: IBM's staggered CFET approach, by shifting the top nanosheets 10nm, saved 20nm in cell height and achieved 40% cell height scaling versus today's non-stacked nanosheets while remaining patternable with existing lithography capabilities; IBM licenses its CFET designs to Rapidus.
insights.speaker: Laura Peters
insights.so_what: IBM's ability to hit 40% cell scaling using existing (not next-gen) lithography is a notable cost advantage, and its licensing relationship with Rapidus positions Rapidus to bring IBM's CFET IP to market as a foundry competitor.
insights.locator: For its CFET designs (which it licenses to Rapidus), IBM is pursuing a sequential approach

insights.claim: Intel is exploring both monolithic CFET flows and a hybrid-substrate approach using (100) silicon for the nFET and (110) crystalline silicon for the pFET joined via layer transfer, achieving a 3x effective mobility gain from pFET-on-(110) stacked on nFET-on-(100); its 2x2 RibbonFETs at 45nm gate pitch use a shared gate with transistor depopulation and design-technology co-optimization to compensate for the resulting performance reduction.
insights.speaker: Laura Peters
insights.so_what: Intel's substrate-orientation trick is a distinctive, hard-to-replicate technical advantage (3x mobility gain) that could differentiate its CFET generation if it can be manufactured at scale by the early 2030s.
insights.locator: The result is a 3X effective mobility gain using pFET on (110) stacked on nFET on (100).

insights.claim: Samsung fabricated 42nm gate-pitch CFETs with triple-stack channels for both transistor types, using a middle dielectric isolation (MDI) region with three different germanium concentration epitaxial layers to enable independent tuning of gate dipole and work-function metal for n- and p-FETs.
insights.speaker: Laura Peters
insights.so_what: Samsung's early triple-stack, 42nm-gate-pitch CFET demonstration is a concrete public data point on how far its process is along relative to competitors, useful for tracking Samsung Foundry's competitive positioning in next-gen logic.
insights.quote: To enable independent tuning of the gate dipole and work-function metal for n- and p-FETs, we introduce three epitaxial layers for the MDI between top- and bottom-tier gate regions,
insights.locator: For example, Samsung fabricated 42nm gate-pitch CFETs

insights.claim: IBM demonstrated high-NA EUV patterning of 21nm metal lines using a single exposure, replacing the more complex first-generation NA EUV self-aligned litho-etch-litho-etch multi-patterning approach, and achieving even better electrical results.
insights.speaker: Laura Peters
insights.so_what: Single-exposure high-NA EUV patterning at 21nm would reduce process steps and cost versus multi-patterning, an important lithography cost lever relevant to ASML's high-NA EUV tool adoption timeline.
insights.locator: Importantly, IBM also demonstrated high-NA EUV patterning of 21nm metal lines

themes.theme: Backside power delivery compounds manufacturing risk

insights.claim: All CFET flows will use backside power delivery according to imec's roadmap, a technique first introduced at the 2nm node that requires advanced wafer bonding, backside thinning, and highly accurate frontside-to-backside alignment, adding significant manufacturing complexity and process-variation sensitivity.
insights.speaker: Laura Peters
insights.so_what: Backside power delivery becoming universal across all CFET flows means yield risk from wafer bonding and alignment tolerances is a shared, unavoidable industry-wide bottleneck, not a vendor-specific one — a systemic risk factor for the whole leading-edge foundry ecosystem.
insights.quote: As demonstrated by companies such as TSMC and Intel, these approaches require advanced wafer bonding, backside thinning, and highly accurate frontside-to-backside alignment processes,
insights.locator: Backside power delivery, first introduced at the 2nm node

insights.claim: Even a two-nanometer misalignment in CFET nanosheet structures can cause a significant manufacturing problem, reflecting the near-zero tolerance for variation at this scale.
insights.speaker: Laura Peters
insights.so_what: The extremely tight tolerance for defects underscores why simulation and process-window mapping (rather than trial-and-error silicon runs) are becoming mandatory, not optional, for CFET development — a tailwind for EDA/process-simulation vendors like Lam Research's Semiverse and similar tools.
insights.quote: When you talk about nanosheets, they are just so small. There’s almost no room for variation,
insights.locator: Joseph Ervin, managing director of Semiverse Solutions at Lam Research

themes.theme: Virtual fabrication and AI as pathfinding tools

insights.claim: Intel's assembly test technology development group is building multi-physics modeling tools that let engineers create a bank of design options at any milestone (e.g., 60% or 90% complete) and choose among a few best options for copper density dispersion, because discovering a warpage or copper-density problem a week before tape-out is too late to fix.
insights.speaker: Laura Peters
insights.so_what: This reveals that predictive multi-physics EDA tooling is becoming embedded directly into the tape-out decision process at Intel, not just used for post-hoc analysis — a structural driver of demand for physics-based EDA/simulation software.
insights.quote: But if you tell me a week before tape-out that a complex product might warp, or copper density variation is too high, it’s too late.
insights.locator: Lalitha Immaneni, vice president at Intel assembly test technology development

insights.claim: Lam Research uses machine learning to map the full process window around a nominal fabrication case by injecting variation across each process step, using known equipment capability data (e.g., deposition thickness, etch depth/selectivity) as model inputs, and is exploring language models to help engineers query the process-integration space directly for manufacturable solutions.
insights.speaker: Laura Peters
insights.so_what: AI-assisted process-window mapping and LLM-based process-integration querying represent a concrete near-term application of AI within semiconductor equipment/process R&D, a productivity lever for Lam Research and peers developing similar tools.
insights.quote: AI gives you another engine to explore this space,

insights.claim: Virtual fabrication and digital twins of fab processes are reducing the number of physical wafers that must be run during process development, cutting cost and time versus physical experimentation.
insights.speaker: Laura Peters
insights.so_what: As CFET complexity rises, the economics increasingly favor simulation-first development, a durable tailwind for TCAD/digital-twin software vendors serving leading-edge logic fabs.
insights.quote: One important application of AI and machine learning is the creation of digital twins that simulate fab operations and process flows, reducing the need for costly and time-consuming physical experimentation,
insights.locator: Douglas Guerrero, senior technologist at Brewer Science

themes.theme: EUV patterning challenges at CFET dimensions

insights.claim: EUV lithography at CFET-relevant dimensions faces shot-noise-driven stochastic defects and line-edge/line-width roughness, along with pattern-collapse risk from taller features needed for higher aspect-ratio etching; EUV underlayers and ion beam etching (IBE) are cited as mitigation techniques.
insights.speaker: Laura Peters
insights.so_what: Persistent stochastic and pattern-collapse challenges at advanced EUV dimensions sustain demand for specialty underlayer materials and etch process innovation (e.g., Brewer Science) as enabling technologies for CFET-era lithography.
insights.locator: EUV patterning faces two problems as a direct result of the low total photon count

themes.theme: Technology trickles down across device platforms

insights.claim: Samsung's Jaihyuk Song noted that gate-all-around technology, first implemented in logic, was subsequently extended to DRAM and then NAND devices, with shared library packs creating synergy across the company's product lines.
insights.speaker: Laura Peters
insights.so_what: This establishes a precedent that CFET, once proven in logic, is likely to migrate into Samsung's memory (DRAM/NAND) roadmap as well, suggesting the technology's addressable impact extends beyond just leading-edge logic chips.
insights.quote: Logic devices at Samsung were the first devices to adopt these technologies, and the same approach was extended to DRAM devices, followed by NAND. By rolling out these innovations across the three basic devices, we not only achieved the primary performance gains but also created library packs that create synergy throughout the entire company.
insights.locator: Jaihyuk Song, corporate president and CTO at Samsung
